 Last Update October 28, 2026, 9:48 PM EDT Trump says Iran 'tapping' US along until election 'not going to help them'
 President Donald Trump said that Tehran wants to make a deal to end the U.S.-Iran war, but "maybe they are waiting for the election or something" and that is "not going to help them."

 The United States has warned several Gulf Arab allies to prepare for a potentially brief but intense military campaign against Iran following the U.S. midterm elections, according to The Wall Street Journal.
 Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched toward Taif by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi forces on Tuesday night, according to the Saudi-led coalition.
 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that Washington is tracking and freezing the Iranian regime's cryptocurrency assets as it moves funds.
 President Donald Trump floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz after himself Tuesday during a rally in Texas, pointing to increased oil flows through the waterway.
 A Tehran revolutionary court sentenced a photojournalist to 26 years in prison, human rights group HRANA said.
 Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian described Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's directive to end the current state of “neither war nor peace” between Washington and Tehran as an important step in shaping Iran's future.
 The Yemeni government's armed forces carried out 749 targeted operations against Houthi military capabilities over 24 hours as part of it's “Dawn of Yemen” offensive.
 The Houthis struck Aden airport, Yemeni government forces said, after the group warned people to evacuate.
 Iran is pressing ahead with its proposed seven-day plan, maintaining close contact with mediators to resolve implementation details in less than a week, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said.
 24 Posts Sort by Newest Oldest incoming update… Coverage for this event has ended.
 13 hours ago Pinned Iran signals potential shift in US standoff as Mojtaba Khamenei calls for new approach 
 Mojtaba Khamenei / Fars / Getty Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday described Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's directive to end the current state of “neither war nor peace” between Washington and Tehran as an important step in shaping Iran's future, according to the Islamic Republic News Agency ( IRNA ).
 Khamenei had reiterated Iran’s conditions for ending the war with the U.S. during a meeting with his security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, a day earlier. 
 The meeting focused on reinforcing national unity and moving beyond the current state of uncertainty and tension. According to the Mehr News Agency , Khamenei described the situation as a “crossroads.”
 As mediation continues, Iran has said the U.S. must lift its blockade of Iranian ports before peace talks can begin. Washington wants Iran to make concessions on its nuclear program.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 7 hours ago Saudi Arabia shoots down Houthi ballistic missile targeting eastern region 
 The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said Wednesday that it intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis that was heading toward Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province.
 “Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the eastern region,” Col. Turki Al-Malki, the official spokesman for the coalition forces, said on X .
 Saudi civil defense officials had issued alerts warning of potential danger in Najran, in southwestern Saudi Arabia, and the Eastern Province. Minutes later, officials said the threat had passed in both areas, Reuters reported.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 7 hours ago US crude oil prices slide below $102 as Middle East conflict fuels market uncertainty 
 Hormuz / Farzad Frames / Getty Images US benchmark crude dropped roughly $1 on Thursday in early morning Asia trading, reducing the prior session's gains as investors balanced supply risks against broader market pressures amid intensifying Middle East conflict, Reuters reported.
 West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 92 cents, or 0.9%, to trade at $101.86 a barrel after touching an intraday low of $101.75. The dip follows a 3% surge on Wednesday, the outlet said.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 8 hours ago Trump says Iran's drone production crippled by lack of electricity amid war 
 President Donald Trump / Fox News President Donald Trump said Wednesday that Iran's military is struggling to produce drones because it no longer has access to electricity, hampering its weapons production amid the ongoing war.
 "Their missiles are still there, but not much less," Trump said at a rally in Ohio.
 "They're drones that they make are having a hard time because they can't get electricity anymore.
 "But and they've been they've you know, this war started.
 "I was listening to a very good congressman last week and he said 'Trump didn't start this war.'"
 "This war was started in 1979 by Iran and killed many, many Americans," he said. "Their favorite weapon was the roadside bomb. That was Soleimani. He's dead, by the way," Trump added.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 9 hours ago Yemen alleges Houthis used toxic shells, secret labs as chemical weapons fears grow 
 Yemen’s information minister, Moammar al-Eryani, said Wednesday that Houthi forces are suspected of using shells containing banned toxic substances.
 The statement came amid reports that authorities in Yemen’s Taiz province demanded a probe into allegations that Houthi weapons contained toxic substances, following reports of people fainting and experiencing breathing difficulties.
 “Field reports from the Al-Aqroud and Kahlan fronts concerning the use by the Iran-backed Houthi terrorist militia of shells suspected of containing prohibited toxic substances represent an extremely dangerous development,” al-Eryani wrote Wednesday on X .
 Al-Eryani also cited reports of chemical substances being smuggled into Yemen from Iran and alleged the existence of “secret laboratories to develop and test toxic substances.”
 Al-Eryani called on the United Nations and relevant international organizations, particularly the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), to take urgent action.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 9 hours ago US Embassy warns of potential airport attacks in Saudi Arabia as Houthi threat grows 
 The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh warned Wednesday of potential attacks on airports and travel disruptions in Saudi Arabia, citing missile and drone attacks by Houthi rebels.
 The State Department had ordered nonemergency U.S. government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia on Oct. 23, 2026, due to safety risks. 
 "Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," the embassy said on X .
 “The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area."
 The embassy also advised "extreme caution" if people choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 10 hours ago Erdogan offers Trump help ending Ukraine war, raises Middle East security concerns 
 Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke with President Donald Trump on Wednesday and offered Ankara's support for efforts to end the war in Ukraine while highlighting ongoing security concerns in the Middle East .
 “President Erdoğan noted that we as the Makkah Joint Defense Alliance closely follow the developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen, and strive for the resolution of the problem on the basis of diplomacy,” the Turkish presidency said in a statement on X .
 Trump also congratulated Turkey on Republic Day and offered best wishes for the upcoming Organization of Turkic States summit.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 10 hours ago Trump denies directing Vance to launch Iran peace talks amid reports of letter to Tehran 
 President Donald Trump / Michael M. Santiago / Getty Images President Donald Trump said Wednesday that he did not direct Vice President JD Vance to initiate peace negotiations with Iran , amid reports that Vance had sent a letter to Tehran to kick-start new talks.
 When pressed on the matter ahead of traveling to a rally in Ohio and Trump replied, "No."
 “No, they need help with medical supplies and various things," he told reporters.
 “He asked me what I thought. I said, if you want to do that, that's okay. Basically, it's getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” Trump clarified.
 The Wall Street Journal reported that Vance had sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in an effort to revive peace negotiations.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 11 hours ago CENTCOM calls Iran's Hormuz sea mine claims 'false,' says shipping routes are clear 
 Claims by Iran that ships have struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz are false, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said Wednesday, adding that the waterway's primary shipping routes are clear.
 “Over recent days and weeks, Iranian-controlled media have reported Iranian claims that commercial vessels are hitting sea mines while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. These claims are FALSE,” the command said on X .
 “All internationally recognized primary transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared of sea mines by U.S. forces and remain so,” CENTCOM said, adding that thousands of commercial vessels have “safely used the transit lanes and continue today.”
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 12 hours ago Netanyahu's bloc projected to win 53 seats, leaving Israel facing political deadlock 
 Netanyahu / Yonatan Sindel / Pool via Reuters Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc is projected to secure 53 Knesset seats after counting nearly 5 million ballots, falling short of a 61-seat governing majority, according to Central Elections Committee data, The Jerusalem Post reported Wednesday.
 Netanyahu’s Likud leads with an expected 26 seats, supported by seven seats each for United Torah Judaism, Shas and Otzma Yehudit, alongside six seats for the Religious Zionist Party.
 Meanwhile, the main opposition bloc, comprising Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar (21 seats), Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid’s B’Yachad (12 seats), the Democrats (eight seats) and Yisrael Beytenu (seven seats), stands at 48 seats, while Arab parties are projected to secure 19 seats, with the Joint List securing 12 and Ra'am taking seven seats.
 The expected outcome leaves Israel facing political deadlock, as neither major Zionist bloc has a viable path to an outright majority without making major ideological concessions, the outlet said.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 12 hours ago Iran sentences photojournalist to 26 years in prison as serious health concerns mount 
 A Tehran revolutionary court sentenced a photojournalist to 26 years in prison, human rights group HRANA said Wednesday.
 The court handed down a 20-year sentence to Artin Ghazanfari for media-related work — double the original 10-year term after the court invoked enhanced espionage penalties — along with five years for "assembly and collusion" and one year for anti-state propaganda.
 Ghazanfari was detained during the January protests, when security forces raided his home and workplace and seized electronic devices, books and professional equipment.
 Rights groups have raised concerns about Ghazanfari's declining health, noting that he suffers from heart failure, asthma and high blood pressure.
 Iranian authorities have blocked his transfer to medical facilities and rejected his family's appeals for temporary medical bail.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 13 hours ago Yemeni military says 239 Houthi fighters, commanders targeted in sweeping offensive 
 The Yemeni government's armed forces carried out 749 targeted operations against Houthi military capabilities over 24 hours as part of it's “ Dawn of Yemen ” offensive, armed forces spokesman Col. Majed al-Nazili said Wednesday.
 The military also targeted 239 Houthi commanders and fighters, he said on X.
 “The strikes targeted field command centers, fortifications, fire positions, reinforcements, and means of movement and supply; which contributed to suppressing sources of fire, disrupting the militia's field command, and depriving its forward positions of support and resupply,” al-Nazili added. 
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 14 hours ago Houthis strike Yemen airport after evacuation warning, leaving civilians injured, flights grounded 
 The Houthis struck Aden airport on Wednesday, Yemeni government forces said, after the group warned people to evacuate.
 According to Reuters , residents in the southern port city, where the Saudi-backed Yemeni government is based, said they heard an explosion near the airport.
 The Yemeni forces said the attack on the airport caused civilian injuries and property damage.
 Air traffic was also halted after the strike, two Transportation Ministry officials told Reuters.
 “The Houthi's repeated targeting of Aden International Airport threatens the safety of civilians, civil aviation, and the delivery of humanitarian aid,” the government said on X .
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 14 hours ago Iran pushes 7-day plan as foreign minister says Tehran remains in contact with mediators 
 Iran is pressing ahead with its proposed seven-day plan, maintaining close contact with mediators to resolve implementation details in less than a week, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday, even as Washington has rejected recent Iranian proposals.
 “While our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed,” he said.
 “We remain in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries to review ideas that can ensure implementation of our 7-Day Plan in even less than a week,” Araghchi added.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 15 hours ago Kuwait summons Iranian ambassador over 'blatant interference' in country's affairs: report 
 Kuwait's Foreign Ministry announced Wednesday that it summoned Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Toutounchi following a statement the Iranian embassy made amounting to "blatant interference in the internal affairs of the State of Kuwait," a report said. 
 The diplomatic dispute began after a Kuwaiti court sentenced three men to death on Monday for collaborating with Iran and Lebanon's Hezbollah terrorist group in an alleged plot to assassinate senior Kuwaiti officials, according to Iran International. 
 The Embassy of Iran in Kuwait then issued a statement Wednesday saying it " categorically rejects the claim put forward by the Kuwaiti government regarding the involvement of one of the Iranian citizens in a plot to assassinate figures or in any other act that would undermine Kuwaiti national security, and reminds that the mentioned individual has not been present in Kuwait during the past ten years." 
 "While expressing its profound regret over the persistence of the negative approach toward Iran, which manifests, among other things, in the repetition of baseless and worn-out scenarios regarding Iran's interference in Kuwaiti affairs, the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Kuwait affirms that directing such unfounded accusations at Iranian citizens contradicts the principle of good neighborliness and violates international laws," the statement added. 
 Kuwait's foreign ministry later said Wednesday that the Iranian embassy statement infringed on the country's sovereignty and judicial independence, Iran International reported. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 16 hours ago Suspect killed following 'terrorist attack' against police officer outside Israeli embassy in Serbia 
 Serbian gendarmes guard the Israeli Embassy after an unidentified assailant attacked a guard with knives in Belgrade, Serbia, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Darko Vojinovic/AP) A knife-wielding suspect was shot and killed in Belgrade, Serbia on Wednesday after allegedly attacking a police officer who was protecting the Israeli embassy there, a report said.  
 Serbia’s Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said police were treating the incident as a “terrorist attack” and had raised the terror threat to the highest level. 
 The officer, who was slightly wounded in the face, responded by fatally shooting the attacker, according to The Associated Press. 
 Dacic described the attacker as a minor who had two knives. 
 He attacked the member of the Gendarmerie, shouting Allahu Akbar, or “God is great” in Arabic, the AP also reported. 
 The Associated Press contributed to this post. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 17 hours ago Military options being prepared for Trump after he says 'anything's possible' with Iran: officials 
 President Donald Trump salutes during the national anthem as he hosts a Columbus Day celebration in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 9, 2026. (Evan Vucci/Reuters) Official and military sources told Fox News on Wednesday that movements are being made in the Middle East to give President Donald Trump options if he decides to resume strikes against Iran.  
 The development comes after The Wall Street Journal reported this week that "the U.S. has told several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military campaign after the U.S. midterm elections," citing people familiar with the conversations. 
 When asked by a reporter about the possibility of the U.S. striking Iran after November's midterms, Trump said late Tuesday, "I can't tell you that... but anything's possible." 
 The Wall Street Journal report said an additional aircraft carrier strike group and Marine expeditionary unit are being repositioned, while the U.S. is bringing a Patriot missile defense system from Texas into Israel to help the Middle Eastern ally bolster its defenses and U.S. forces in the region are restocking their munitions, among other moves. 
 The sources told Fox News that the movements being reported are to make sure the U.S. military is ready if asked to do something by Trump, but there is no indication the president has made a decision yet. 
 Trump has telegraphed possible likely targets in Iran, such as its Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site and Kharg Island, although Trump also has called off major strikes six times since July. 
 Fox News' Jennifer Griffin contributed to this post. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 18 hours ago Egypt, Saudi Arabia looking to prevent Iran-backed Houthis from escalating aggression 
 Iran-aligned Houthi fighters fire from their position in a screengrab from a video said to show Houthi fighters attacking Saudi-backed forces in al Jawf governorate, Yemen, on Sept. 15, 2026. (Houthi Military Media/Reuters) The foreign ministers of Egypt and Saudi Arabia held a phone call this week to discuss efforts "to contain the current crisis and prevent escalation," according to Egypt's Foreign Ministry. 
 The call unfolded Tuesday, the same day Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched toward Taif by Houthi forces. 
 Egypt's Foreign Ministry said the call between Badr Abdelatty and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan "addressed the latest regional developments, efforts to contain the current crisis and prevent escalation, the likelihood of which has increased recently, and working to advance political and peaceful solutions through dialogue." 
 On Monday, Egypt's parliament allowed President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to take "all necessary measures" to help Saudi Arabia defend itself, according to Reuters. 
 Fox News Digital's Emma Bussey contributed to this post.  
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 18 hours ago Iran warns Israel against a 'military misadventure' in the Persian Gulf region 
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Israel should not pursue a "military misadventure" in the Middle East. 
 Araghchi made the comment on X as he shared an image of him standing alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) Summit in Moscow, Russia. 
 "Iran’s energy diplomacy advanced at GECF Summit. Discussions focused on global gas markets and energy security," Araghchi said. "Devastating impact on international markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure in Persian Gulf region remains major concern for both gas suppliers and consumers." 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 20 hours ago Israel, US have chance to 'remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all,' Netanyahu says 
 Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks to his supporters at Likud party headquarters in Jerusalem after the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Ohad Zwigenberg/AP) Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday that his country and the U.S. have a chance to remove the Iranian threat "once and for all," a report said. 
 Netanyahu, during a speech at the Lukid party election headquarters in Jerusalem, pushed for the formation of "a strong, right-wing national government," according to Reuters. 
 "Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all. But ulterior motives must not divert us from this sacred mission," he reportedly said. 
 Netanyahu's political bloc gained ground Wednesday morning as Israel counted votes from its first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre, but remained short of the majority needed to form a government, leaving the country facing another potential political deadlock. 
 With approximately 70% of votes counted, Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc stood at 54 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 47 for the main opposition and 19 for Arab parties, according to partial election results reported by Israeli media. Netanyahu's Likud led with 27 seats, while former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party held 20. 
 Fox News' Efrat Lachter contributed to this post.
